correctness.rationale: The exact Poisson-binomial variance gives at most 2n distinct exponential modes in the derivative. An explicit Rolle-induction bounds derivative zero multiplicity by 2n-1. At rates 20^(j-1), negative witnesses at log(4)/lambda_j and positive witnesses at log(2)/(2lambda_j) alternate chronologically and have rigorously signed contributions by inequalities 1/19<1/8, 1-1/sqrt2>1/4, and sum_{k>=1}20^k 2^(-10*20^(k-1))<40/1024<1/20. These produce 2n-1 distinct simple roots for all n; 110 finite programmatic sign checks were replayed but are not the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Classical exponential Chebyshev bounds are acknowledged, not claimed new. The all-n sharp constructive attainment and robust high-mode variance behavior under the exact independent exponential ecological survivor-count model were not implied by any inspected full-text primary item, related scholarly comparison or indexed result. The complete Engen (2007) text remained inaccessible and is recorded as a residual priority risk; no absence-of-hit uniqueness claim is made.
residual_risks: Full Engen (2007) text was inaccessible despite OA/preprint searches and authorized institutional attempt; an equivalent previously published extremum bound cannot be definitively excluded.
Full Fox–Kendall (2002) material was not retrieved; its abstract concerns a different individual-level variance problem.

Classical general exponential-polynomial oscillation bounds are acknowledged; other treatments of constrained exponential-mixture modes might subsume the explicit sharp construction under alternate terminology.
No independent external expert/bibliographic audit was performed.

value.rationale: The variance of independently surviving species richness is a natural temporal community-uncertainty statistic, unlike mean richness it can increase and decrease repeatedly. The exact n-peak upper bound and robust all-size sharp construction settle a meaningful temporal shape question for finite heterogeneous exponential extinctions, including the sharp two-species onset of bimodality. Scope and empirical limitations are stated.
